mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (or equivalent) of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese Notary Public, then Legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC, then Consular Legalization by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) in the relevant jurisdiction (since Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, consular legalization is mandatory; no apostille is applicable).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent) for the parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR or local Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese Notary Public, then Legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC, then Consular Legalization by TECO (parallel path to apostille; consular legalization is the sole route for Taiwan).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the Taiwan JV and appointing the local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chinese parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese Notary Public, then Legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC, then Consular Legalization by TECO (no apostille applicable).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese Notary Public, then Legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC, then Consular Legalization by TECO (consular path only).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Taiwan FSC's published sanctions list. Additionally, screening against the PRC's List of Persons Subject to Anti-Money Laundering Supervision and the PBOC's Beneficial Owner Registry. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP (domestic or foreign), including family members and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily via automated systems), and upon any trigger event. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. For high-risk jurisdictions, additional enhanced measures include source of wealth verification and senior management approval. The protocol must comply with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations and the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Company Registration and Name Clearance System (Taiwan Company Name Pre-Approval Portal) operated by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) of Taiwan
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. English names are optional but must be transliterated phonetically or semantically consistent with the Chinese name. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) trade name (distinctive part), (2) business type (e.g., Limited Company), (3) industry description (optional), and (4) legal form suffix (e.g., Co., Ltd.). The Chinese name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. For foreign-invested enterprises, the English name must be a direct transliteration or translation of the Chinese name, and both must be submitted for clearance. The MOEA will reject names that are misleading, contrary to public order, or contain prohibited tokens.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: R.O.C. Companies Act (公司法): Articles 1, 128–153, 387–388; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例); Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People; Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions (電子支付機構管理條例), Articles 6, 8, 9, and FSC enforcement rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company and Commerce Registration Online Application System; delegated municipal commercial bureaus.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) accompanied by the approved Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, board minutes, and the Investment Commission approval letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital under the Companies Act; however, the FSC mandates paid-in capital of no less than NT$500 million (approximately USD 16.5 million) for an Electronic Payment Institution purely issuing corporate virtual cards. The subscribed capital must be deposited and held in a Taiwan commercial bank escrow account in the Company's name until CPA verification and registration are completed. The FinTech Innovation Experimentation Act (Regulatory Sandbox) can temporarily waive this threshold for a limited-time pilot.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. RESOLVED: (1) the allotment of the subscribed shares to the foreign investor and domestic partner, together with the paid-up capital lodged in the escrow account, be ratified; (2) the registered office at [address], Taipei, be adopted; (3) [Name] be appointed Chairman, [Name] appointed General Manager, and [Name] appointed Chief Compliance Officer; (4) the officers are authorized, jointly and severally, to execute the incorporation application, open corporate bank accounts, and apply for the FSC electronic payment institution license; (5) this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce — Company Name and Business Scope Pre-check System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked candidate company names and the approved business scope wording via the MOEA online portal; the system issues an automatic preliminary approval valid for six months. Ensure the name does not duplicate an existing company and does not contain prohibited bank or financial terms before the FSC license is granted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, the system states the collision reason; file a new application with alternate candidates within the same session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Investment Commission (投資審議委員會)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the investment application under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (foreign partner) and the Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People (PRC partner). The approval letter fixes the shareholding percentages and must be obtained before company registration; the approved amount is the total JV capital contribution.
required_dossiers: Joint venture contract and shareholders' agreement
Audited financials and incorporation certificates of each investor
Power of attorney and identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Investment Commission deficiency letter within 30 days; one extension is available; amend the JV structure if sector-level restrictions on mainland capital are imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of Incorporation Drafting and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court Notary Office or licensed notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with Companies Act Article 129 mandatory items, obtain the promoters' subscription minutes and first board resolution, and notarize the signatures of all subscribing shareholders. Certified Chinese translations must accompany foreign-language documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notary returns the set for re-execution if any mandatory article is missing; amend and re-notarize without refiling the name pre-check.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce / delegated municipal commercial bureaus
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Establishment Registration Application online with scanned documents, pay the NT$4,000 registration fee plus NT$300 name-check fee and NT$1,000 Investment Commission application fee, and upload the CPA's paid-in capital verification. The issuance of the company registration certificate constitutes the legal creation of the JV.
required_dossiers: CPA capital verification report and bank escrow certificate
Registered office usage consent with building owner's notarized consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, cure all listed defects within 15 days and re-submit through the same portal; a second rejection requires full refiling but does not void the name clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance (BLI); National Health Insurance Administration (NHIA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File taxpayer registration to obtain the Taxpayer Identification Number and uniform invoice number for VAT; register the company as an employer with BLI for labor insurance and labor pension, and with NHIA for national health insurance. Complete within 15 days of the registration certificate issuance; failure triggers penalties.
required_dossiers: Employment roster and labor pension plan
Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct conflicting identity or address records at the respective counter; the registration number remains valid pending correction of supplementary data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSC Electronic Payment Institution License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the license application under the Act Governing Electronic Payment Institutions, including the business plan for corporate virtual expense cards on Mastercard and Visa rails, the AML/CFT policy, risk management framework, card product terms, and proof that the NT$500 million paid-in capital is maintained. After the FSC issues the business license, apply to the international card networks for BIN sponsorship.
required_dossiers: FSC license application form and business plan
AML/CFT manual and risk control procedures
Capital adequacy certificate and bank proof
Overseas parent company joint venture guarantee letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the FSC deficiency memo within 60 days; for capital-related objections, restore paid-in capital to NT$500 million or apply for temporary sandbox authorization under the FinTech Innovation Experimentation Act to continue limited issuance during the cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau (金融監督管理委員會銀行局)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Payment Institution Business License (電子支付機構營業執照) — Corporate Virtual Expense Card Issuance on Mastercard and Visa rails

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (環境部), formerly Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Only / Low Impact Office-Based Financial Service — not included in the development categories requiring a full EIA report; qualifies as exempt with general environmental management duties
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic sanitary wastewater must meet the public sewer or Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards; no process wastewater generated. Office waste, retired payment hardware and data media must be handled through licensed recyclers under the Waste Disposal Act, with chain-of-custody certificates for card destruction. No process VOC emissions; HVAC refrigerants must comply with the National Fluorocarbon Substance Management Regulations and the Montreal Protocol; card personalization outsourcing overseas removes local emission liability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate and evacuation plan approval from the municipal Fire Bureau under the Fire Services Act; structural load inspection and certificate of occupancy issuance under the Construction Act for the registered office; Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace clearance and emergency response drills completed before business launch; public liability insurance and business continuity plan for the card processing and data storage rooms maintained in force.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains strict separation between current account and capital account convertibility. Current account items, including trade-related payments and service fees, are generally freely convertible upon presentation of authentic supporting documents. Capital account items, including foreign direct investment equity injections, cross-border loans, and repatriation of invested capital, remain subject to a comprehensive approval, filing, or registration regime administered by SAFE. Profit remittance by a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is permitted only after the JV has completed audited annual accounts, satisfied all applicable PRC corporate income tax liabilities, and appropriated mandatory reserve funds (statutory surplus reserve and, if applicable, discretionary reserves), with remittance effectuated via a SAFE-licensed bank under a Foreign Exchange Payment of Dividends registration/filing. Non-resident shareholders face documentary hurdles including tax certificates from competent Chinese tax authorities under the tax treaty clearance procedures, anti-money laundering source-of-funds verification, and in some jurisdictions, proof of beneficial ownership transparency. Virtual card issuing is treated as a payment-related information service for FX purposes; quarterly data submissions to SAFE are mandated where receipts or payments connected to cross-border card settlement flows exceed specified thresholds. Conversion limitations apply to Renminbi outflows within the onshore market; currency swaps and FX forwards must be executed through banks qualified as onshore derivatives dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE framework, there is no mandatory full surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Export receipts in foreign currency must be repatriated to China within the statutory timeframe stipulated by SAFE uniform rules, generally no later than 30 days to 90 days after the date of export customs declaration, depending on the type of goods and mode of settlement. The JV must process receipt verification through the cross-border trade monitoring system. For current account receipts, the JV is permitted to retain foreign currency in its designated current account or convert into Renminbi at pilot bank rates, but the bank and SAFE must monitor the authenticity and matching of the underlying trade, including receipts related to B2B virtual card acquiring settlements classified under cross-border service trade. If the JV issues virtual cards to corporate clients that load RMB funds and spend via Mastercard or Visa networks outside China, the outbound settlement to the international card schemes is characterized as cross-border payment service settlement requiring a legitimate RMB purchase and payment purpose code that reflects the payment institution's merchant acquiring or card issuance service; the JV is typically required to be a licensed cross-border payment institution and must maintain residual FX exposure within prescribed limits, with any short positions closed through onshore banks under forward FX or spot FX sale contracts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Currenxie, and MultiPass are not licensed as deposit-taking banks in China and cannot serve as the JV's primary treasury settlement rail for RMB current accounts or FX regulatory compliance. Their viability is low to medium only as ancillary disbursement nodes for non-RMB vendor payments, provided the payments are not deemed payment services into China. Cross-border fintech payment institutions must hold a non-bank payment institution license from PBOC, a cross-border payment operator recordal under SAFE, and satisfy cybersecurity multilevel protection (MLPS) schemes. Foreign EMIs acting as a bank-agnostic card issuing programme manager for PRC-domiciled JV accounts would trigger unlicensed cross-border payment operations unless they partner with a fully licensed PBOC-affiliated clearing institution such as UnionPay International or a licensed bank sponsor under the card association's principal membership rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the JV's legal representative and, in practice, the financial controller or compliance officer is required at the bank's counterparty risk interview and for signing of corporate account opening instruments. Remote account opening is not permitted widely for a newly established Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture classified as a high-risk payment-related business. Authorized directors that are non-Chinese residents should expect to attend, in person, at least one onboarding session at the branch where the account is domiciled, alongside provision of notarized board resolutions and apostilled or PRC-consular legalized corporate documents. Digital verification of passport, residence permit, and board-mediated electronic bank signing is possible after the physical interview has occurred, but cannot fully replace the first meeting for the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BNI (Beneficial Ownership Information) deficiency for foreign investors in the JV, particularly if the ultimate beneficial owner is a private equity fund or complex regional holding structure with opaque nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and PRC-legalized group structure chart; certified shareholder register; UBO declaration forms (PBOC form) with names, nationality, ID numbers, and proof of funding source; certificate of good standing from the home registry; audited financial statements of each material intermediate entity; board resolution identifying the natural-person UBO; and independent legal opinion confirming no nominee or undisclosed control arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model scores high risk under PBOC AML rules: virtual card issuance is not a traditional regulated financial institution in China unless licensed as a card-clearing institution or bank payment aggregator, and card loads from multiple unrelated corporate clients trigger money laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PBOC-issued payment business license; card association sponsor agreement with a licensed bank card clearing institution; SAFE cross-border payment filing; transaction monitoring system description; AML/CFT internal control manual approved by the board; risk-based customer due diligence policies; sanctions screening policy; auditable audit trail on card load and spend; independent audit report under ISO 20022 / PCI DSS for card data security.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital contribution, with non-resident corporate shareholders in tax-haven jurisdictions or low corporate substance jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the remitting bank; source-of-funds certificate from the shareholder's auditor; legalized board resolution approving the FDI capital injection; specific SAFE foreign exchange business registration (FDI) proof, and proof that the capital contribution was made through the capital account with a genuine business purpose and no round-tripping of Chinese-source funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sandbox or license-pending status exposes the JV to a money service business classification not recognized by some Tier 1 banks, which might treat it as an unlicensed payment institution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written regulatory comfort letter or no-action letter from PBOC or local PBOC branch, applying for a Payment Business License under Administrative Measures for Payment Services of Non-Financial Institutions (PBOC Order [2010] No. 2, as amended 2023); detailed road map showing the timeline for license approval; legal opinion on the permissibility of B2B virtual card interoperability with Mastercard/Visa while the JV acts as a sponsor bank's White Label issuer; evidence of contractual sponsorship by a licensed bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential violation of circular 64/2013 regarding cross-border guarantee or cash pooling structures when the JV uses parent-funded liquidity or internal financing through virtual card load accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE cross-border guarantee registration; full amounts and direction of each guarantee documented; capital account transaction history; inward/outward remittance purpose codes; FID (Foreign Investment Information) report; and a transfer pricing and thin capitalization analysis demonstrating arm's-length interest rates and adequate capitalization under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 46.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from foreign shareholders into the JV must be routed through the shareholder's direct remittance in a freely convertible foreign currency into the JV's SAFE-designated capital account at a Tier 1 bank. Each injection must be declared under SAFE's Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration, including the FDI business registration with the market regulator and SAFE's capital project information system. The remittance must use purpose code 'China-FDI injected capital' (under SAFE's business codes for balance of payments, generally current code 6220 or 6221, depending on whether it is equity injection or further contribution), and the receiving bank verifies the capital account quota within the amount approved by the FDI registration. Use of offshore RMB from a foreign shareholder is permitted only if the RMB qualifies as foreign currency in fact and is transferred via a RMB settlement account under the Cross-Border RMB Settlement framework, requiring no formal SAFE approval for current account but still requiring FDI registration for equity contribution; all audit and anti-round-tripping verification applies. Shareholder loans should be placed separately and require SAFE foreign debt registration, including the quota calculation, to avoid illegal cross-border financing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for virtual card program-related spend, merchant payouts, and software/data processing service fees should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct bank transfers, with letter of credit (commercial LC) used for high-value goods procurement related to card personalization and hardware where suppliers demand documentary guarantees. Each outbound disbursement requires a genuine trade or service contract, invoice, customs declaration (when goods), and SAFE-approved payment purpose codes in the cross-border payments system. For virtual card load settlements to Mastercard or Visa, the JV must clear via a sponsor bank settlement account and may use MT103 from that bank to the card association's settlement bank. The sponsor bank will report to SAFE through the International Payments System (SWIFT) with payment purpose code '221000' (telegraphic transfer of foreign currency) or the specific service trade code for payment network clearing services if offered by a licensed institution. Commercial LC disbursements should be denominated in USD or EUR and issued by the Tier 1 domestic bank against insurance of underlying B2B purchase orders; no direct RMB LC for non-trade virtual card top-up is permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts with a licensed commercial bank under real demand principle, covering actual current account receivables and payables from virtual card load and card settlement flows

FX swaps (foreign exchange swap transactions) between RMB and USD/EUR with onshore banks for intermittent working capital mismatches, subject to genuine risk exposure and SAFE approved derivatives documentation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for offshore parent entities protecting the consolidated balance sheet, but only through the offshore shareholder and not through the Chinese JV, as PRC-regulated institutions are currently subject to NDF prohibition; the JV can only access onshore forwards with deliverable settlement
Currency options on real trade exposures where the bank's risk rating and PBOC derivative qualification apply, only with physical delivery of the underlying currency at maturity

Cross-currency swaps executed as part of a qualified FX swap facility with the sponsor bank, with each swap supported by an underlying FX obligation in relation to future Mastercard/Visa settlement outflows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders’ meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; no routine filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) solely to approve the statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, subject to statutory extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting or comply with directors’ duties may result in statutory liability and fines; no automatic annual-return strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed and paid by May 31 following the fiscal year; extensions may apply under applicable rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, underpayment, or nonpayment may trigger tax assessments, interest, and statutory penalties; persistent noncompliance does not follow a standard annual-return strike-off timetable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed every two months by the 15th day of the following filing period; applicable filing frequency and exemptions depend on taxpayer status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing and late payment may trigger statutory penalties, interest, and tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner information update, if reportable information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA company beneficial-owner information reporting platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 15 days after a reportable change; confirm current reporting scope and exceptions for the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or update may result in statutory fines and follow-up orders; no routine annual strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement filing or regulatory report, if required by company status or financial-sector license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA or the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Depends on whether the company is publicly listed, regulated, or holds a financial-sector license; verify the applicable license-specific reporting calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: May include administrative fines, corrective orders, or license restrictions; consequences depend on the applicable statute and license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Taiwan companies generally require CPA audit and certification when statutory criteria apply, including paid-in capital of at least NT$30 million; listed companies and regulated financial institutions are subject to additional requirements. A virtual-card or payment business may require separate FSC authorization and license-specific audit and reporting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan private-company GAAP generally applies to non-public companies; TIFRS applies to specified public-interest and listed entities. The applicable framework depends on company status and sector-specific regulation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a universal annual shareholder-register confirmation filing. Report beneficial-owner information and changes through the MOEA platform when required, within the applicable reporting period. Maintain an up-to-date shareholder register and record share transfers and corporate changes; confirm any license-specific annual certification requirements.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–2,500 per year; commercial provider fees vary, and Taiwan companies do not generally have a mandatory registered-agent renewal fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–20,000 or more per year; varies materially by size, complexity, and financial-sector licensing

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax (effective for 2018 and later assessment years; reduced from 17% pre-2018). A 5% surcharge on undistributed retained earnings under Income Tax Act Article 21-1 increases the maximum aggregate effective cost on accumulated profits to approximately 25%. For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in virtual card issuing, the assessed tax base is global net income with a credit/wHT offset mechanism for foreign-source income; profits arising from the Taiwan card scheme, interchange, processing and programme management fees are fully Taiwan-source and taxable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available for fintech card-issuing operations. Applicable reducing mechanisms: (a) Research-and-development expenditure investment tax credit of up to 20% of qualifying R&D costs under the Act for Industrial Innovation, capped at 30% of the income tax payable in each of the applicable years; (b) Angel-investor credits and SME investment credits under the Act for the Development of Small and Medium Enterprises, inapplicable to a large JV; (c) the Financial Technology Development and Innovative Experimentation Act (FinTech Regulatory Sandbox) grants temporary licensing relief but no rate reduction; (d) the 5% retained-earnings surcharge can be eliminated by declaring full dividend distribution; (e) export-linked tax incentives are unavailable; the practical effective rate for a JV distributing all after-tax profits is 20%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 - Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), together with Form 15-B (Retained Earnings Surcharge Return), Form 23-P (Business Income Tax Payable Statement) and statutory schedules including the Transfer Pricing Disclosure Statement (移轉訂價揭露表) and Related-Party Transaction disclosures. Mandatory electronic filing through the National Taxation Bureau E-Filing Portal (電子申報繳稅服務網, https://tax.nat.gov.tw) using the company digital certificate (工商憑證) or an approved B2B security token; paper filing is available only to taxpayers with no data-interface capability and is treated as a higher audit-risk category.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, supported by three provisional quarterly advance-payment instalments of estimated tax due on 30 June, 30 September and 31 December of the income year; a fourth balancing payment is made with the annual return. Estimates are self-assessed; underpayment of the provisional instalments by more than one-third attracts an annualised interest addition.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final balance of tax must be filed and paid within five months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year JV (the normal rule for a Taiwan incorporated entity) the deadline is 31 May of the following year. No blanket filing extension is granted; a technical extension may be approved only in documented disaster or system-outage situations and must be requested in advance through the E-Filing Portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 01 - 營業收入淨額 (Net Operating Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate net revenue from virtual corporate card issuing: scheme fees, interchange earned on B2B transactions, card programme management fees, account-servicing charges, foreign-exchange conversion margins, and settlement spread. Revenue must be reported gross before intercompany cost allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file this line; the Taiwan JV reports all Taiwan-source card revenue attributable to the local issuing licence. Revenue derived from cards used by foreign cardholders travelling in Taiwan remains Taiwan-source and is fully reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 02 - 營業成本 (Cost of Operations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs: network assessment fees payable to Mastercard/Visa, settlement and clearing charges, card production and tokenisation costs, bank sponsor fees, and direct personnel costs allocated to the issuing operation. Costs must be evidenced by third-party invoices and intercompany agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost recharges paid to the foreign sponsor bank or the mainland Chinese technology parent are deductible only to the extent they satisfy the arm's-length standard and are substantiated with Taiwanese-documented invoices or certificate-of-expense proof; the cost line must exclude the 20% withholding taxes and any royalty-type payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 04 - 營業費用及損失總額 (Operating Expenses and Losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, administration, depreciation, amortisation, research and development, and intercompany service fees. For a fintech JV, major components are software amortisation, licensing fees, cybersecurity expenses, and salaries; entertainment expenses and donations are subject to statutory caps.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees paid to the foreign parent/affiliates require a Service Charge Agreement and a benefits test; intellectual-property royalties paid to a related non-resident are subject to 20% withholding and must be supported by a royalty valuation report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10/11 - 營業淨利 / 非營業收益及損失 (Operating Profit / Non-Operating Income and Losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income derived outside the core issuing operations: foreign-exchange gains, interest on cardholder deposits, dividends from strategic investments, and gains on disposals of software. Losses include foreign-exchange losses and realised bad debts of cardholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source dividend income from an offshore holding company holding the card scheme's treasury assets is separately reported and may qualify for the foreign-income exemption only if the foreign subsidiary meets the substantial-activity test under the CFC regime and the Article 43-3/43-4 rules; otherwise it is taxed with a foreign-tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income before tax after statutory adjustments: disallowance of non-arm's-length intercompany charges, entertainment caps, CFC inclusions, reversal of prior-year loss carryforward deductions (maximum 10 years), and deduction of tax-exempt items such as domestic dividends and qualifying foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder has no line on this return; the JV must exclude any income attributable to a permanent establishment of the foreign partner. Profit-shifting structures that divert Taiwan card revenue to a Hong Kong or BVI affiliate will be recharacterised by the tax authority under Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 56 - 營利事業所得稅額 (Income Tax at 20%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax on taxable income at 20%, before investment tax credits and foreign-tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable directly; however any tax withheld at source by the Taiwan JV on outbound dividends to the mainland Chinese shareholder is recorded separately and remitted under Form 15 withholding schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 57-59 - 投資抵減及扣繳稅額 (Credits and Tax-Withheld Adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible items include certified R&D investment credits (20% of qualifying expenditures, capped at 30% of tax), foreign tax credits on foreign-source income, and income tax withheld at source on Taiwanese interest and dividends received by the JV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available only to the Taiwan taxpayer of record; the mainland/JV parent cannot claim Taiwanese R&D credits on the Taiwan entity's return. Foreign tax credit claims require a verified statement of the foreign tax paid and are capped by the Taiwan tax on the corresponding foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 60/61 - 應自行繳納之營利事業所得稅 (Self-Assessed Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after deducting the three provisional instalments, current-year withholding credits, and investment credits. This is the amount surrendered with the return by 31 May.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder bears no filing obligation for the JV's corporate tax. However, if the JV fails to file, the tax authority is authorised to collect against the foreign parent as a controlling shareholder in cases of corporate-shield abuse.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% of the assessed tax when filed within two weeks after the deadline; 15% when filed within one month; plus 2% for each additional month or part thereof, capped at 30% in total (Income Tax Act Article 108). Late payment: surcharge of 1% for every two days of delay, capped at 15%, plus statutory interest at the one-year postal savings deposit rate (Tax Collection Act Article 20). Non-filing after a tax authority demand notice: three times the assessed tax. Fraudulent understatement (Article 110): penalty of between 1 and 2 times the undercharged tax depending on degree of concealment; deliberate evasion carries criminal liability. Every error triggering underpayment accrues daily interest until payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% gross on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder (Income Tax Act Articles 88 and 73-2). A mainland Chinese corporate shareholder receives the same 21% rate because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement of 2015 is signed but not ratified and confers no binding withholding relief. An additional 5% retained-earnings surcharge is payable by the JV on any undistributed net profits for each assessment year. Dividends paid to Taiwanese-resident corporate shareholders are exempt under Article 42 and are not subject to withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Negotiate DTA relief only where the shareholder is a tax resident of a jurisdiction with a comprehensive Taiwan tax treaty. The sequence is: (1) Obtain an original Certificate of Residence (居住者證明, the Taiwan functional equivalent of a TRC) from the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, certifying residence in the year of the dividend; (2) complete Form for Application for Income Tax Treaty Benefits (申請適用所得稅協定相關申請書) together with a Beneficial Ownership Declaration and evidence of corporate substance (office, staff, decision-making); (3) submit both documents to the Taiwan JV before the dividend record date; the JV as withholding agent files the application with the local National Taxation Bureau before the remittance date to obtain a reduced or exempt withholding approval; (4) where the standard 21% was already withheld, the shareholder must apply for a refund with the certificate package within the five-year statutory refund window. Treaty rates applicable to a Chinese-controlled JV are irrelevant because no China-Taiwan DTA is effective; a Hong Kong intermediate holding company will be struck down on beneficial-ownership and substance grounds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross rates: royalties on intellectual property paid to a non-resident 20%; interest paid to a non-resident 20% (Income Tax Act Articles 88 and 92). Comprehensive treaty rates are typically 10% for royalties and 10% for interest (e.g., Japan, The Netherlands, Singapore); certain treaties reduce interest to 5% for financial institutions and royalties to 5% for industrial or copyright property. No treaty reduction is available for royalties or interest paid to mainland Chinese related parties; therefore intercompany licensing from the Chinese parent at 20% gross and intercompany loans at 20% gross create an effective statutory cost of 40% on every currency unit remitted. The JV as withholding agent must withhold within 10 days of payment and remit by the 10th day of the following month; failure to withhold or remit triggers a penalty of one to three times the unwithheld tax plus daily interest (Article 114).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: TWD 20,000,000 per related-party transaction category (e.g., separate thresholds for card platform services, software licensing, funding/loans, management fees) triggers mandatory attachment of the Transfer Pricing Disclosure Statement (移轉訂價揭露表) to the Form 15 annual return. A full Local File (移轉訂價報告) is mandatory where the same-category controlled transactions exceed TWD 50,000,000 in the aggregate, or where the entity has transactions with a tax-haven company irrespective of amount, or where the taxpayer has persistent operating losses while paying related-party fees; the Local File must be provided to the tax authority on demand within one month. Master File (集團主檔報告) is mandatory when the group's consolidated revenue in the preceding year reached TWD 30,000,000,000 and the Taiwan entity's related-party transaction amount is TWD 150,000,000 or more (or its related-party revenue reached TWD 30,000,000). Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where the group's consolidated revenue in the preceding year reached TWD 27,000,000,000 and the Taiwan entity meets the related-party transaction or revenue threshold. Documents must be prepared in Traditional Chinese; English originals require certified translation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan is not a zero-tax offshore jurisdiction and OECD Economic Substance Regulations do not apply to a Taiwan-incorporated JV. Equivalent substance and anti-abuse doctrines apply with equal force: (a) General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Income Tax Act Article 43-1 permits the tax authority to recharacterise any arrangement lacking business purpose and economic substance; (b) the CFC regime (Articles 43-3 and 43-4, effective for 2023 calendar-year profits) attributes to the JV the undistributed income of any controlled foreign company - including a Hong Kong or BVI intermediate - that fails the substantial-activity test performed through the Taiwan entity's own substance; (c) treaty benefit application requires certification of beneficial ownership and actual economic presence of the recipient (no flow-through conduits); (d) the FinTech card-issuing licence itself demands permanent office premises, locally resident senior management, risk-management and compliance personnel in Taiwan under the Electronic Payment Institution Act, so the JV cannot be a booking-only shell without losing its FSC licence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Taiwan-source scheme, interchange and card programme revenue from Form 15; inflating cost of operations with fabrications; shifting profits to a Hong Kong or BVI shell via excessive management fees or circular royalty payments lacking arm's-length comparability; filing loss returns while the mainland parent receives payments; destroying or refusing relevant digital transaction logs after a tax examination notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full tax undercharged plus daily interest at the one-year postal savings rate; civil penalty of 2 times the understated tax for intentional evasion (1 time for gross negligence) under Article 110; where a demand notice is issued and ignored, 3 times the assessed tax; criminal prosecution under Tax Collection Act Article 41: imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to TWD 1,000,000; in aggravated cases the court may order forfeiture of unexplained assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person(s) - including the JV general manager and the mainland-appointed director who actually managed daily operations - are exposed to arrest and criminal conviction; the corporate veil may be pierced under Company Act Article 154(2) where shareholder abuse of the corporate form causes serious harm to the revenue, making the shareholder personally liable for the unpaid tax; exit restrictions under Tax Collection Act Article 24 apply when overdue tax exceeds TWD 1,000,000, prohibiting the director from leaving Taiwan until the arrears are settled or security is provided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorised card issuing and unlicensed e-payment business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the virtual corporate card programme - including issuing Mastercard/Visa BIN products, holding cardholder funds, settling transactions, or providing stored-value payment functionality - without the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) licence under the Electronic Payment Institution Act, or exceeding the limited scope of a FinTech Regulatory Sandbox approval; using a purely contractual 'card-agent' label to disguise the true principal card issuer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability with imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to TWD 50,000,000 under the Electronic Payment Institution Act penalties for unlicensed operation; the FSC concurrently issues a cease-and-desist order, orders the return of all cardholder deposits, and may impose administrative fines of TWD 5,000,000 per violation on the institution; the card network may terminate BIN sponsorship, materially destroying the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board of directors and the mainland shareholder company are jointly and severally liable for restitution of cardholder funds; the persons who authorised each unlawful card issuance face personal criminal exposure; unpaid administrative fines escalate to compulsory execution against personal assets; the responsible person is subject to travel restriction pending FSC administrative enforcement; directors who knowingly participated in the unlicensed scheme are barred from serving as officers or directors of any Taiwanese financial institution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards without an effective anti-money-laundering (AML) programme: failure to perform customer due diligence and know-your-business screening on the ultimate beneficial owners of corporate cardholders; processing loads or transactions for sanctioned entities, shell holding vehicles, or unauthorised money-service businesses; failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) on structured reloading patterns; failure to appoint a compliance officer and to conduct annual independent AML audit mandated for regulated e-payment institutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, administrative fines from TWD 500,000 up to TWD 10,000,000 per violation with an additional fine per day of continued non-compliance; the FSC may revoke the e-payment licence and order withdrawal of senior managers; criminal liability for knowingly assisting a money-laundering scheme carries imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to TWD 50,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The AML compliance officer and the responsible directors who disregarded statutory CDD obligations are personally liable for administrative fines where willful blindness is established; criminal conviction of a director for money-laundering facilitation triggers immediate travel bans, disqualification from company management, and confiscation of the criminal proceeds; personal injury claims from defrauded cardholders are actionable directly against directors who allowed the use of the card platform for fraudulent disbursement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company intermediation, economic-substance abuse and cross-strait investment circumvention
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Taiwan JV profits to the mainland Chinese parent through a Hong Kong or BVI intermediate that performs no economic functions, holds no employees or offices, and exists solely to convert what is economically a dividend into 'management fees', 'IT services' or 'brand royalties', thereby evading the 21% dividend withholding tax; structuring mainland-capital control of the JV without the required Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) approval for mainland investment in a financial-sector entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment under Article 43-1 reclassifies the circular payments as constructive dividends, with 21% withholding imposed at the JV level; penalties of 1 to 2 times the under-withheld tax; the mainland investor faces MOEA order to dispose of its stake within a fixed period and fines of up to TWD 2,500,000 for unapproved investment; in aggravated cases MOEA may order dissolution of the JV and cancellation of the FSC e-payment licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the circular royalty or management-fee structure are personally and jointly liable for the unwithheld 21% tax and the accompanying penalties; the mainland-appointed chairman is subject to an exit ban while the assessment is pending; must show that the Hong Kong/BVI vehicle has real substance without which the DTA or exemption claim is invalid; criminal charges under the Tax Collection Act Article 41 may be brought against directors for the fraudulent conversion into fee income; the corporate veil will be lifted against both the JV and its foreign intermediate owners resulting in recovery against the ultimate mainland shareholder's Taiwanese assets.
